title: A finite set in a scheme with an ample invertible sheaf lies in an affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an ample invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For every finite set $E\subseteq X$ there exists an affine open $U\subseteq X$ with $E\subseteq U$.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-ample-proj-open] there are a nonnegatively graded commutative ring $S$ and an open immersion $X\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]; identify $X$ with its image, an open subscheme of $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$. Let $\overline X$ be the closure of the underlying set of $X$ in $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ and put $T=\overline X\setminus X$. Since $X$ is open, $T=\overline X\cap(\operatorname{Proj}(S)\setminus X)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01ZY proof, first paragraph: Proposition 01Q3 gives an open subscheme of Proj

proof.text: For each point of the finite set $E$, the basis statement [lem-sc-proj-standard-open-basis] gives a positive-degree homogeneous element $f_i$ such that the corresponding $D_+(f_i)$ contains that point and is disjoint from $T$. Taking the finitely many choices gives $E\subseteq\bigcup_iD_+(f_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(S)\setminus T$.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01ZY proof, second paragraph: standard opens form a basis and E is finite

proof.text: Let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the graded ideal they generate. If $E=\{\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_m\}$ in $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, then $I$ is contained in none of the homogeneous primes $\mathfrak p_j$. The graded prime-avoidance statement [lem-sc-graded-prime-avoidance] therefore gives a positive-degree homogeneous $f\in I$ outside every $\mathfrak p_j$, so $E\subseteq D_+(f)\subseteq\bigcup_iD_+(f_i)$.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01ZY proof, third paragraph: apply Algebra Lemma 00JS to I and the point primes

proof.text: Since $X$ is open in $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, $U=X\cap D_+(f)$ is an open subscheme of $D_+(f)$. Because $D_+(f)\cap T=\varnothing$, $U=\overline X\cap D_+(f)$ as sets, so $U$ is also closed in $D_+(f)$. The inclusion $j:U\to D_+(f)$ is then a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]: it is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, and $\mathcal O_{D_+(f)}\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is surjective, being an isomorphism over the open set $U$ and having zero target over the open complement $D_+(f)\setminus U$. By [lem-sc-proj-standard-open-basis], $D_+(f)$ is affine, and a closed immersion is an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism], so $U=j^{-1}(D_+(f))$ is affine. Thus $U$ is an affine open of $X$ containing $E$.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01ZY proof, final paragraph: D_+(f) affine and X cap D_+(f) closed in it (closedness argued topologically, X being open)
